question: According to the manual, which of the following is a recommended way to avoid becoming a distracted driver?
choice_a: Program the GPS while merging onto the highway
choice_b: Review maps, program the GPS, and plan your route before you begin driving
choice_c: Engage in complex or emotionally intense conversations with passengers to stay alert
choice_d: Keep a snack in hand at all times in case you get hungry
explanation: The manual advises drivers to 'Review maps, program the GPS and plan your route before you begin driving,' and separately warns against eating/drinking while driving and against complex or emotionally intense conversations with occupants.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: How does the manual define road rage?
choice_a: Operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others or physically assaulting a driver or their vehicle
choice_b: Driving slowly in the left lane of traffic
choice_c: Any instance of driving 10 mph or more over the posted speed limit
choice_d: Failing to signal a lane change in heavy traffic
explanation: The manual states, 'Road rage is operating a motor vehicle with the intent of doing harm to others or physically assaulting a driver or their vehicle.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: Which of the following does the manual suggest to reduce your stress before and while you drive?
choice_a: Use gestures to let other drivers know how you feel
choice_b: Follow closely behind slow drivers to encourage them to speed up
choice_c: Drive slowly in the left lane to set a calm pace
choice_d: Listen to 'easy listening' music
explanation: The manual lists 'Listen to "easy listening" music' as a way to reduce stress, while separately advising drivers not to drive slowly in the left lane, to avoid gestures, and to keep a reasonable following distance.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: What does the manual say you should do first and foremost if confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Make eye contact so they know you see them
choice_b: Flash your high beams at them
choice_c: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_d: Speed up to hold your position in the travel lane
explanation: The manual states, 'First and foremost, make every attempt to get out of their way,' and separately advises against holding your lane and against making eye contact.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: Why does the manual caution against wearing dark or tinted corrective lenses while driving at night?
choice_a: They cut down the light you need to see clearly under night driving conditions
choice_b: They are illegal in all states after sunset
choice_c: They fog up more easily than clear lenses
choice_d: They increase the glare produced by your own headlights
explanation: The manual states that tinted lenses 'cut down the light that you need to see clearly under night driving conditions,' even if a driver thinks they help with glare.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: Per the manual, roughly how far will a vehicle traveling 55 mph travel during just two seconds of glare blindness?
choice_a: Less than 5 feet
choice_b: About one car length
choice_c: More than half the distance of a football field
choice_d: About 10 feet
explanation: The manual states, 'Even two seconds of glare blindness can be dangerous. A vehicle going 55 mph will travel more than half the distance of a football field during that time.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: About how far ahead can a driver typically see when using low-beam headlights, according to the manual?
choice_a: About 100 feet
choice_b: About 1,000 feet
choice_c: About 500 feet
choice_d: About 250 feet
explanation: The manual states, 'With low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet and with high beams about 350-500 feet.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-27

question: NHTSA estimates cited in the manual attribute roughly how many police-reported crashes a year to drowsy driving?
explanation: The manual states, 'NHTSA estimates that 100,000 police-reported crashes a year are the result of drowsy driving.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a warning sign of fatigue that should tell you to stop and rest?
choice_a: Faster reaction time
choice_b: Increased appetite
choice_c: Trouble remembering the last few miles driven
choice_d: Feeling unusually calm and relaxed
explanation: The manual lists 'Trouble remembering the last few miles driven; missing exits or traffic signs' among the warning signs of fatigue that should prompt a driver to stop and rest.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-26

question: The manual states that getting six hours of sleep or less before driving does what to your crash risk?
choice_a: Doubles your risk
choice_b: Cuts your risk in half
choice_c: Triples your risk
choice_d: Has no measurable effect
explanation: Under 'Are You At Risk?' the manual lists being 'Sleep-deprived or fatigued (6 hours of sleep or less triples your risk).'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-26

question: What does the manual recommend using for the best visibility when you must drive in fog?
choice_a: High-beam headlights only
choice_b: Low-beam headlights and fog lights
choice_c: Parking lights only
choice_d: No headlights, so they don't reflect off the fog
explanation: The manual advises drivers in fog to 'Use low-beam headlights and fog lights for best visibility even in daytime, and be alert for other drivers who may have forgotten to turn on their lights.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-29

question: After crossing deep standing water that has wetted your brakes, what does the manual say to do once you're out of the water?
choice_a: Maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out
choice_b: Pump the parking brake rapidly until it feels normal
choice_c: Immediately accelerate to highway speed to dry the brakes with airflow
choice_d: Pull over immediately and wait 30 minutes before moving again
explanation: The manual instructs, 'When out of the water, maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out,' then to make a test stop when safe.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-30

question: What distinguishes a passive railroad crossing from an active one, according to the manual?
choice_a: A passive crossing has flashing lights but no gates
choice_b: A passive crossing is found only on rural roads
choice_c: A passive crossing always has a posted stop sign
choice_d: A passive crossing has no type of traffic control device, leaving the decision to stop or proceed entirely up to the driver
explanation: The manual states, 'Passive Crossings. This type of crossing does not have any type of traffic control device. The decision to stop or proceed rests entirely in your hands.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-31

question: If there is no white stop line painted on the pavement, how close to the nearest rail must a vehicle that is required to stop position itself?
choice_a: Exactly 100 feet
choice_b: No closer than 5 feet and no more than 25 feet
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no more than 50 feet
choice_d: As close as possible without touching the rail
explanation: The manual states that if there is no white stop line, 'vehicles that are required to stop must stop no closer than 15 feet or more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of the nearest track.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-32

question: Which of the following is NOT listed by the manual as a factor in selecting a 'safe' speed for a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: Steepness of the grade
choice_b: Color of the vehicle
choice_c: Total weight of the vehicle and cargo
choice_d: Weather
explanation: The manual lists total weight, length of the grade, steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather as factors in choosing a safe downgrade speed; vehicle color is not one of them.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-33

question: Using the manual's example, if your 'safe' speed on a downgrade is 40 mph, at what speed do you apply the brakes and to what speed do you slow before releasing them?
choice_a: Apply at 50 mph, release at 45 mph
choice_b: Apply at 35 mph, release at 30 mph
choice_c: Apply at 40 mph, release at 35 mph
choice_d: Apply at 45 mph, release at 40 mph
explanation: The manual's example states, 'if your "safe" speed is 40 mph, you would not apply the brakes until your speed reaches 40 mph. You now apply the brakes hard enough to gradually reduce your speed to 35 mph and then release the brakes.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: What are escape ramps built on steep mountain downgrades designed to do?
choice_a: Stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers
choice_b: Allow vehicles to bypass weigh stations
choice_c: Provide a shortcut around slow-moving traffic
choice_d: Cool overheated brakes before continuing downhill
explanation: The manual states, 'Escape ramps are made to stop runaway vehicles safely without injuring drivers and passengers,' using a long bed of loose, soft material.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: What is 'counter-steering,' as described in the manual's discussion of emergency steering?
choice_a: Steering with only one hand to react faster
choice_b: Braking hard while turning to slow the vehicle faster
choice_c: Turning the wheel back in the other direction once you've passed the obstacle
choice_d: Turning the wheel as sharply as the vehicle will allow
explanation: The manual defines counter-steering as being 'prepared to "counter-steer," that is, to turn the wheel back in the other direction, once you've passed whatever was in your path.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: If your path is blocked on both sides during an emergency, which direction does the manual recommend steering?
choice_a: It does not matter which direction you choose
choice_b: Left, because oncoming traffic will yield
choice_c: Straight through whatever is blocking you
choice_d: Right, so you don't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and cause a head-on collision
explanation: The manual states, 'If you are blocked on both sides, a move to the right may be best. At least you won't force anyone into an opposing traffic lane and a possible head-on collision.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: Which emergency stopping method has you apply the brakes all the way, release them when the wheels lock up, and reapply them as soon as the wheels start rolling again?
choice_a: Engine braking
choice_b: Controlled braking
choice_c: Stab braking
choice_d: Progressive braking
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as: 'you apply your brakes all the way and release brakes when wheels lock up. As soon as the wheels start rolling, apply the brakes fully again.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-35

question: On a vehicle with hydraulic brakes, what does the manual say to remember when using the parking/emergency brake to slow the vehicle after losing hydraulic pressure?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake only after the vehicle has already stopped
choice_b: Shift into the highest gear available first
choice_c: Pump the parking brake pedal rapidly
choice_d: Press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time so you can adjust the brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up
explanation: The manual states that when using the parking brake to slow the vehicle, 'be sure to press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time you use the emergency brake so you can adjust the brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-36

question: What does the manual say you should do with the brake pedal immediately after a tire fails?
choice_a: Pump the brake rapidly to alert following traffic
choice_b: Brake as hard as possible to stop before losing control
choice_c: Apply the brake only on the side with the failed tire
choice_d: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, then brake very gently
explanation: The manual states, 'Stay off the Brake... Unless you're about to run into something, stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down. Then brake very gently, pull off the road, and stop.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-36

question: Per the manual, the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after which date?
choice_a: March 1, 2000
choice_b: March 1, 1995
choice_c: March 1, 1999
choice_d: March 1, 1997
explanation: The manual states ABS is required on 'Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-37

question: Which of the following statements about ABS is TRUE, according to the manual's safety reminders?
choice_a: ABS will not prevent skids caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn
choice_b: ABS replaces the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_c: ABS will always shorten your stopping distance
choice_d: ABS allows you to follow other vehicles more closely
explanation: The manual states, 'ABS won't prevent power or turning skids—ABS should prevent brake-induced skids or jackknifes, but not those caused by spinning the drive wheels or going too fast in a turn.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-38

question: The manual lists four causes of skids. Which of the following is one of them?
choice_a: Over-acceleration, which supplies too much power to the drive wheels and causes them to spin
choice_b: Turning on your headlights in daylight
choice_c: Using cruise control on a highway
choice_d: Driving with underinflated steer tires
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration ('Supplying too much power to the drive wheels, causing them to spin'), and driving too fast as the four causes of skids.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-38

question: What is the first step in correcting a drive-wheel braking skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel as sharply as possible
choice_b: Apply the parking brake immediately
choice_c: Accelerate hard to regain traction
choice_d: Stop braking, to let the rear wheels roll again
explanation: The manual states, 'Stop Braking. This will let the rear wheels roll again, and keep the rear wheels from sliding,' followed by counter-steering.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-39

question: What is the first thing the manual says to do at an accident scene when you are not seriously hurt?
choice_a: Exchange information with the other driver
choice_b: Take photographs for insurance purposes
choice_c: Move all vehicles off the roadway regardless of injuries
choice_d: Keep another accident from happening in the same spot
explanation: The manual states, 'The first thing to do at an accident scene is to keep another accident from happening in the same spot,' which is done by protecting the area with flashers and reflective triangles.
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-39

question: Why does the manual say you should keep the doors shut on a cargo fire in a van or box trailer?
choice_a: Because open doors void the vehicle's insurance coverage
choice_b: To keep the fire visible to other drivers
choice_c: To keep smoke from setting off nearby smoke alarms
choice_d: Because opening the van doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast
explanation: The manual states, 'For a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, keep the doors shut, especially if your cargo contains hazardous materials. Opening the van doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast.'
source_note: AR CDL Manual (AAMVA 2022 Modernized Testing System, Version: March 2025), Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-40
